title: Anomaly Decomposition & Compact Dashboard Guidelines
summary: Practical guidance for building compact, high-signal dashboards and a repeatable anomaly decomposition workflow for inference services. Focuses on metric naming/semantics, low-cardinality tracing attributes, widget design, and triage steps to localize root cause with minimal noise.
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a set of heuristics and concrete conventions for:
- defining metrics and spans used for inference anomaly triage,
- designing compact dashboards that prioritize signal-to-noise for oncall and SRE use,
- an ordered decomposition workflow to locate root cause quickly when an alert fires.

Scope and audience:
Primary audience: SREs, runtime engineers, and engineers instrumenting model serving paths (hosted/Dedicated/Private).
This is intentionally prescriptive where possible (metric names, units, low-cardinality label sets) and advisory for UX/layout choices.

Why a compact dashboard?
We repeatedly see dashboards with too many high-cardinality group-bys and widgets that turn triage into a scavenger hunt. A compact dashboard should:
- show the minimal set of signals that answer the triage question "Is this an application/configuration issue, or an infrastructure/host problem?"
- provide immediate drilldowns while keeping default view low-cardinality and curated.

Principles (short):
- Low-cardinality defaults: limit top-level widgets to 3-4 labels (region, model_family, tier).
- High-signal metrics only: prefer percentiles + error rates + queue depth over infinite custom gauges.
- Use derived rate counters (per-second) not cumulative counters in widgets where slope matters.
- One primary latency SLI (p95 for user-facing, p99 for batch) and one primary reliability SLI (request_error_rate).
- Trace anchors: standard span names and a minimal attribute set to join traces with logs/metrics.

Metric naming and canonical definitions (recommended):
Note: metric names are suggestions; keep them snake_case and service-prefixed where possible (service_inference_*).
- service_inference_request_count (counter)
  - unit: requests
  - description: total inference requests received by the front proxy per minute
  - labels: region, model_family, deployment_tier

- service_inference_error_count (counter)
  - unit: errors
  - description: errors returned to callers (4xx and 5xx differentiated in label error_class)
  - labels: region, model_family, deployment_tier, error_class

- service_inference_latency_seconds (histogram)
  - unit: seconds
  - description: end-to-end request latency (ingress -> final response)
  - buckets: exponential up to 30s; use pre-aggregated percentiles (p50,p90,p95,p99) in dashboards
  - labels: region, model_family, deployment_tier, route

- service_kv_cache_hit_ratio (gauge)
  - unit: fraction [0,1]
  - description: rolling fraction of requests that used KV/prefix cache to avoid full decoding
  - labels: model_family, deployment_tier

- inference_queue_depth (gauge)
  - unit: items
  - description: number of requests queued at the serving runtime (per gRPC worker pool)
  - labels: host_pool, region, model_family

- kv_cache_evictions_per_minute (counter)
  - unit: evictions/min
  - description: rate of KV cache evictions (indicator of cache thrash)
  - labels: model_family, cache_tier

Label cardinality guidance:
- region: small (us-west, us-east, eu-central)
- model_family: limited to top-level families (gpt-medium, gpt-large, emb-only) not per-model-version on default dashboards
- deployment_tier: hosted|dedicated|private
- route: only when routing differences matter (e.g., streaming vs non-streaming)
- host_pool: use aggregated pools, not individual hostnames on default view

Tracing conventions (practical):
Span naming pattern (short and consistent):
- inference.request (root span created at ingress)
- inference.decode
- inference.kv_lookup
- inference.attention_compute
- inference.kernel_dispatch
- inference.response_serialize

Required span attributes (keep these low-cardinality and stable):
- service.instance_id (string, aggregated pool id)
- model_family
- model_variant (optional for rollout debugging)
- request_id (unique id)
- route
- user_tier (free|paid|enterprise)
- host_pool

Sampling and size guidance:
- Keep sampling at ~1-2% globally but implement dynamic ramp-on for errors and anomalies: when an error rate alert triggers, increase sampling to 100% for the affected model_family + region scope for 10 minutes.
- Always capture full traces for requests that cross a latency or error threshold via a trace-filtering hook.

Dashboard layout and widget guidance (compact defaults):
Top row (1 line): Health overview (single-row):
- small heatmap or sparkline for request_rate (per region), p95 latency (global), error_rate (global).
- status pill for controlled rollouts (deployments with canary percent > 0 show canary status).

Primary row: Root cause triage widgets (3 widgets):
1) Latency distribution (p50/p90/p95/p99) aggregated by model_family (stacked area compact)
2) Error rate (per-second) by error_class (client|validation|infrastructure) with anomaly shading
3) Queue depth and worker utilization (dual axis) aggregated by host_pool

Secondary row: Supporting signals (3 widgets):
- KV cache hit ratio (trend) + evictions per minute as sparkline
- Incoming request size distribution (to catch prompt injection/spike in token length)
- Trace-sampled slowest spans (list of top-10 sampled traces by latency with link to full trace)

Widget design rules:
- Each widget default: max 5 series. If underlying cardinality >5, show top-5 with an explicit "more" drilldown.
- Use percentile lines not raw histograms for higher-level views.
- Prefer relative change shading (small/medium/large) instead of absolute colors to highlight anomalies across scales.
- For error rates, show absolute count in tooltip and percent in y-axis.

Anomaly decomposition workflow (step-by-step):
1) Validate alert: check alert rule and time window, compare to deploys/changelogs.
2) Look at top-row overview: is this primarily latency or error?
3) If latency: open Latency distribution by model_family. If one family is responsible -> switch to that family drilldown.
4) Check KV cache hit ratio and evictions: if hit ratio dropped and latencies increased, suspect cache thrash or key mismatch due to a rollout.
5) If errors: open error_class breakdown. If infrastructure errors dominate, check host_pool utilization and worker OOMs. If client/validation errors dominate, check request sizes and recent schema changes.
6) Pull traces (link from widget): inspect slowest span name to see whether time is spent in attention_compute vs kernel_dispatch vs serialization.
7) If attention_compute is the hotspot and GPU util is low, suspect kernel mismatch/quantization fallback or wrong kernel selection. Check kernel selection logs (linked artifact).
8) If host_pool shows high CPU or memory, open infra dashboards and escalates to SRE if capacity exhaustion suspected.

Example PromQL-ish snippets (pseudocode):
- p95 latency for a model_family: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(service_inference_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model_family))
- error rate per second: sum(rate(service_inference_error_count[5m])) by (error_class)
- kv cache hit ratio (rolling): avg_over_time(service_kv_cache_hit_ratio[15m]) by (model_family)

Checklist for engineers instrumenting new routes or models:
- Add service_inference_request_count and service_inference_error_count counters with labels: region, model_family, deployment_tier
- Ensure latency histogram is exported with appropriate bucket ranges and that percentiles are computed at ingest (or via pre-aggregation)
- Emit kv_cache_hit boolean or counter so the ratio can be derived (avoid high-cardinality cache_key label)
- Add required trace attributes (model_family, host_pool, request_id) to root span
- Implement trace-filtering hook to force-capture slow/error requests
- Add one small dashboard entry (widget) to the compact dashboard via PR when the route goes live

Operational runes and heuristics (quick wins):
- If p95 spikes but kv_cache_hit_ratio fell by >10 percentage points in last 10m, treat as cache regression and rollback recent model_variant changes.
- If p99 increases while GPU_util is unchanged and kernel_dispatch latency spikes in traces, consider swapping quantization profile or forcing a kernel to reproduce.
- If queue_depth increases while request_rate is flat, suspect a downstream stall (e.g., redis or async DB) rather than more load.

Example open questions / TODOs:
- Should we standardize a single percentiles export pipeline vs computing in dashboards? (cost vs accuracy tradeoff)
- How to automate dynamic sampling increases for affected scopes without exploding trace storage? (prototype/infra ticket needed)
- Define canonical model_family taxonomy: current labels are inconsistent across teams. Action: product/ops to propose mapping.

Appendix: common triage links and quick references:
- Trace viewer query template: /traces?service=inference&filter=model_family:{model_family}%20AND%20span.duration:>1s
- Telemetry config repo (metrics + buckets): https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-config
- Alert runbook stub: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Alert+Runbook+Template

Notes to self / meeting friction points (raw):
- Need to socialize the low-cardinality defaults with the platform team; some teams want per-model-version labels which will break dashboard clarity.
- We should add a widget generator that can create curated drilldown dashboards per model_family automatically, using the same templates.

End.

(If this doc is useful, I will convert key sections into a checklist PR for telemetry-config and a small dashboard template in grafana/dashboards repo.)
